title: Covariates: Implicit Weights and Covariate Balance
text: two_period_aipw_weights() AIPW. outcome model includes 2000 levels covariates change police; setting pscore_formula = ~1 pscore_d_covs_formula = ~1 (covariates propensity score) gives regression adjustment. Every covariate outcome model balanced exactly, levels changes. weightsname argument adds sampling weights, extra_balance_vars_formula reports balance covariates model.  Two diagnostics worth reporting alongside balance. ess element effective sample size comparison group implicit weights (see effective_sample_size()): weights concentrated units, smaller . ggtwfeweights(..., plot_relative_to_target = TRUE) shows whether weights also move treated group away covariate distribution.

title: Covariates: Implicit Weights and Covariate Balance
text: States adopted stand--ground laws different years, full panel staggered adoption. group variable now first year state treated (0 never treated sample).
code: castle$G <- BMisc::get_group(castle, "sid", tname = "year", treatname = "post") table(castle$G[castle$year == 2000]) #>  #>    0 2006 2007 2008 2009 2010  #>   29    1   13    4    2    1

title: Covariates: Implicit Weights and Covariate Balance
text: implicit_twfe_weights() decomposes TWFE coefficient weighted comparisons treated group never-treated group year. base_period = "gmin1", comparison uses year group first treated base period, ::att_gt(). summary() splits estimate. alpha post part comes post-treatment comparisons; pta violations bias part comes pre-treatment comparisons, close zero parallel trends holds treatment. TWFE estimate comes pre-treatment comparisons. twfe_cov_bal() adds balance statistics covariates, averaged time within state first. summary plot average post-treatment cells:
code: twm <- implicit_twfe_weights(   yname = "l_homicide", tname = "year", idname = "sid", gname = "G",   xformula = ~ l_police + unemployrt, base_period = "gmin1", data = castle ) #> Warning in title: Covariates: Implicit Weights and Covariate Balance
text: implicit_aipw_weights() estimates overall average treatment effect treated, ATToATT^o, AIPW regression adjustment group post-treatment year, combines Callaway Sant’Anna (2021). states timing group, propensity score hard estimate, regression adjustment natural choice . Covariates xformula enter level base period (g−1g-1), ::att_gt(); d_covs_formula adds change since base period. Without d_covs_formula, estimate equals ::att_gt() covariates est_method = "reg", aggregated ::aggte(type = "group").  Comparing two balance plots shows covariates estimator balances, well. comparison covariates, outcome model balance check, way see sensitive estimate covariates enter.

code: wo <- attO_weights(attgt) ws <- att_simple_weights(attgt)  c(   TWFE = sum(tw$weights_df$weight * tw$weights_df$attgt),   ATT_o = sum(wo$weights_df$weight * wo$weights_df$attgt),   ATT_simple = sum(ws$weights_df$weight * ws$weights_df$attgt) ) #>        TWFE       ATT_o  ATT_simple  #> -0.03654894 -0.03101828 -0.03995128 aggte(attgt, type = "group", bstrap = FALSE)$overall.att #> [1] -0.03101828 aggte(attgt, type = "simple", bstrap = FALSE)$overall.att #> [1] -0.03995128 comparison <- data.frame(   group = tw$weights_df$group,   time.period = tw$weights_df$time.period,   post = tw$weights_df$post,   attgt = tw$weights_df$attgt,   TWFE = tw$weights_df$weight,   ATT_o = wo$weights_df$weight,   ATT_simple = ws$weights_df$weight ) comparison[comparison$post == 1, ] #>    group time.period post        attgt        TWFE      ATT_o ATT_simple #> 2   2004        2004    1 -0.010503246  0.04571981 0.02617801 0.06872852 #> 3   2004        2005    1 -0.070423158  0.04571981 0.02617801 0.06872852 #> 4   2004        2006    1 -0.137258739  0.03248687 0.02617801 0.06872852 #> 5   2004        2007    1 -0.100811363 -0.01085101 0.02617801 0.06872852 #> 9   2006        2006    1 -0.004594607  0.19730313 0.10471204 0.13745704 #> 10  2006        2007    1 -0.041224472  0.11062737 0.10471204 0.13745704 #> 15  2007        2007    1 -0.026054411  0.57899403 0.68586387 0.45017182 ggtwfeweights(wo)

title: Implicit Weights and Covariate Balance for Difference-in-Differences Estimators
text: Estimate ATT(g,t)ATT(g,t) ::att_gt(), using never-treated group universal base period, pass result twfe_weights():  post-treatment cells get negative weight, pre-treatment cells get non-zero weight. attO_weights() att_simple_weights() give weights behind ATToATT^o ATTsimpleATT^{simple} comparison.
code: library(twfeweights) data(mpdta, package = "did")  attgt <- did::att_gt(   yname = "lemp", tname = "year", idname = "countyreal",   gname = "first.treat", data = mpdta,   control_group = "nevertreated", base_period = "universal",   bstrap = FALSE, cband = FALSE ) tw <- twfe_weights(attgt)  # the weighted sum of ATT(g,t) is the TWFE coefficient sum(tw$weights_df$weight * tw$weights_df$attgt) #> [1] -0.03654894 mpdta$D <- 1 * (mpdta$year >= mpdta$first.treat & mpdta$first.treat > 0) coef(fixest::feols(lemp ~ D | countyreal + year, data = mpdta)) #>           D  #> -0.03654894  ggtwfeweights(tw)

code: data(castle, package = "causaldata") castle <- as.data.frame(castle) castle$G <- BMisc::get_group(castle, "sid", tname = "year", treatname = "post")  twm <- implicit_twfe_weights(   yname = "l_homicide", tname = "year", idname = "sid", gname = "G",   xformula = ~ l_police + unemployrt, base_period = "gmin1", data = castle ) twm <- twfe_cov_bal(twm, ~ l_police + unemployrt + poverty + l_income) ggtwfeweights(twm)

title: Weights behind the overall average treatment effect \(ATT^o\) — attO_weights
text: Computes weights group-time average treatment effect, \(ATT(g,t)\), deliver overall average treatment effect \(ATT^o\) Callaway Sant'Anna (2021): first average \(ATT(g,t)\) group's post-treatment periods, average across groups group size. "group" aggregation ::aggte().

title: Weights behind the overall average treatment effect \(ATT^o\) — attO_weights
code: attO_weights(   attgt_res,   w = NULL,   keep_untreated = FALSE,   weightsname = attgt_res$DIDparams$weightsname )

title: Weights behind the overall average treatment effect \(ATT^o\) — attO_weights
text: attgt_res result ::att_gt(). w Optional external unit-specific weights, one per row attgt_res$DIDparams$data. NULL (default), weights come weightsname. keep_untreated Logical. TRUE, keep rows never-treated group (whose weights \(ATT(g,t)\) zero) results. Default FALSE. weightsname Name column holding time-invariant sampling weights. Defaults weightsname passed ::att_gt(). NULL means unweighted. Ignored w supplied.

title: Weights behind the overall average treatment effect \(ATT^o\) — attO_weights
text: object class mp_weights_obj; see twfe_weights(). weight holds \(ATT^o\) weights.

title: Weights behind the overall average treatment effect \(ATT^o\) — attO_weights
text: weight post-treatment cell \((g,t)\) \(P(G = g | G \neq 0)\) divided number post-treatment periods group \(g\); weights pre-treatment cells zero. weights non-negative sum one. Comparing weights twfe_weights() shows TWFE regression reweights building blocks.

title: Weights behind the overall average treatment effect \(ATT^o\) — attO_weights
text: Callaway, Brantly Pedro H. C. Sant'Anna. "Difference--Differences Multiple Time Periods." Journal Econometrics 225.2 (2021). doi:10.1016/j.jeconom.2020.12.001

title: Weights behind the overall average treatment effect \(ATT^o\) — attO_weights
code: data(mpdta, package = "did") attgt <- did::att_gt(   yname = "lemp", tname = "year", idname = "countyreal",   gname = "first.treat", data = mpdta,   control_group = "nevertreated", base_period = "universal",   bstrap = FALSE, cband = FALSE ) wo <- attO_weights(attgt) sum(wo$weights_df$weight * wo$weights_df$attgt) #> [1] -0.03101828  # same as the group aggregation in did did::aggte(attgt, type = "group", bstrap = FALSE)$overall.att #> [1] -0.03101828

Time-varying covariates enter level base period (\(g-1\)), ::att_gt(); time-invariant covariates can also included. Default ~1. d_covs_formula One-sided formula time-varying covariates entered change base period, \(X_t - X_{g-1}\). Default NULL. pscore_formula One-sided formula covariates propensity score model. Defaults d_covs_formula. extra_balance_vars_formula Ignored; balance computed afterwards aipw_cov_bal(). Present arguments match two_period_aipw_weights(). extra_balance_d_vars_formula Ignored, extra_balance_vars_formula. balance_d_vars_post Ignored, extra_balance_vars_formula. data panel data.frame long format. Unbalanced panels balanced first (warning rows dropped). weightsname Name column holding sampling weights, must constant time within unit. Default NULL (unweighted). ... used.

title: Implicit weights from a TWFE regression with covariates and staggered adoption — implicit_twfe_weights
text: Decomposes coefficient treatment indicator two-way fixed effects (TWFE) regression covariates, y ~ D + covariates | unit + time, weighted comparisons treated group never-treated group time period (Caetano Callaway, 2024). weights within comparison show regression reweights units, twfe_cov_bal() reports well balance covariates.

title: Implicit weights from a TWFE regression with covariates and staggered adoption — implicit_twfe_weights
code: implicit_twfe_weights(   yname,   tname,   idname,   gname,   base_period = "first_period",   xformula = NULL,   data,   weightsname = NULL )

title: Implicit weights from a TWFE regression with covariates and staggered adoption — implicit_twfe_weights
text: yname Name outcome variable. tname Name time period variable. idname Name unit identifier. gname Name group variable: first period unit treated, 0 never-treated units. base_period Base period comparison: "first_period" (default) "gmin1" (period group \(g\) first treated). xformula One-sided formula covariates TWFE regression, e.g. ~ x1 + x2. Time-varying covariates enter levels, regression. Default NULL (covariates). data panel data.frame long format. Unbalanced panels balanced first (warning rows dropped). weightsname Name column holding sampling weights, must constant time within unit. Default NULL (unweighted).

title: Implicit weights from a TWFE regression with covariates and staggered adoption — implicit_twfe_weights
text: object class decomposed_twfe: list est TWFE coefficient treatment indicator. decomposition_est \(\sum w(g,t) \Delta(g,t)\), estimate without remainder terms. decomposition_remainder \(\sum w(g,t) r(g,t)\). pt_violations_bias contribution pre-treatment comparisons, \(\sum_{t < g} w(g,t) \Delta(g,t)\). twfe_gt list one element per \((g,t)\) cell holding g tp (1, 2, ..., T scale), alpha_weight, weighted_outcome_diff, remainder, implicit weights treated comparison units (weights_treated, weights_comparison) comparison group's effective sample size ess. idname, tname, gname, weightsname, data inputs, kept twfe_cov_bal().

title: Implicit weights from a TWFE regression with covariates and staggered adoption — implicit_twfe_weights
text: treated group \(g\) period \(t\) (including pre-treatment periods), function computes weighted average change outcomes base period group \(g\) minus never-treated group, weights coming residual regression (double-demeaned) treatment (double-demeaned) covariates. TWFE coefficient $$\alpha = \sum_{g,t} w(g,t) \big[ \Delta(g,t) + r(g,t) \big],$$ \(w(g,t)\) alpha_weight, \(\Delta(g,t)\) weighted_outcome_diff \(r(g,t)\) remainder element twfe_gt. Weights post-treatment cells sum one. Pre-treatment comparisons also enter estimate; contribution reported pt_violations_bias. base_period = "first_period" remainders zero; base_period = "gmin1" comparison uses period \(g-1\) base period, like ::att_gt(), remainder terms typically small. Covariates collinear (double-demeaned) values dropped; example, time-invariant covariates drop unless interacted time, ~ x + .factor(year) * .factor(region). Without covariates (xformula = ~1) base_period = "gmin1", comparison equals \(ATT(g,t)\) ::att_gt() (universal base period) alpha_weight equals weights twfe_weights().

Either choice results post-treatment estimates ATT(g,t)'s.  pre-treatment periods, using varying base period amounts computing pseudo-ATT treatment period comparing change outcomes particular group relative comparison group pre-treatment periods (.e., pre-treatment periods setting computes changes period t-1 period t, repeatedly changes value t) universal base period fixes base period always (g-anticipation-1).  compute pseudo-ATT(g,t)'s pre-treatment periods, rather reports average changes outcomes period t (g-anticipation-1) particular group relative comparison group.  analogous often reported event study regressions. Using universal base period normalizes estimate period right treatment (earlier user allows anticipation) equal 0, one extra estimate earlier period. xformula formula covariates included TWFE regression. @return gt_weights object data name data.frame contains data weightsname name column containing sampling weights. set, observations weight. weights time-invariant (constant within unit across periods), fix_weights options produce identical results special handling needed. weights vary across time (e.g., time-varying population sizes), default behavior differs panel type: Balanced panel 2x2 comparison uses weight earlier two time periods involved. post-treatment cells, base period (g-1). pre-treatment cells base_period="varying", pre-treatment period . panel DRDID estimators used. what: Log ratio of standard deviations — log_ratio_sd
title: Log ratio of standard deviations — log_ratio_sd
text: Computes log ratio standard deviation covariate treated group standard deviation untreated group, optionally applying estimation weights. unit-free balance statistic compares spread two distributions (Imbens Rubin, 2015); zero spreads equal.

title: Log ratio of standard deviations — log_ratio_sd
code: log_ratio_sd(   x,   D,   est_weights = rep(1, length(x)),   sampling_weights = rep(1, length(x)) )

title: Log ratio of standard deviations — log_ratio_sd
text: x numeric vector. D binary vector, 1 treated 0 untreated units. est_weights numeric vector weights estimation procedure (e.g., implicit regression AIPW weights). Default rep(1, length(x)) (unweighted). sampling_weights numeric vector sampling weights. Default rep(1, length(x)).

title: Log ratio of standard deviations — log_ratio_sd
text: number: \(\log(sd_1) - \log(sd_0)\).

title: Log ratio of standard deviations — log_ratio_sd
text: Imbens, Guido W. Donald B. Rubin. Causal Inference Statistics, Social, Biomedical Sciences. Cambridge University Press (2015).

title: Log ratio of standard deviations — log_ratio_sd
code: set.seed(1) D <- rep(c(1, 0), times = c(20, 80)) x <- rnorm(100, sd = 1 + D) log_ratio_sd(x, D) #> [1] -0.02304912

what: Changes since the GitHub development version
title: twfeweights 1.0.0
text: package now licensed GPL-3 (previously MIT). Removed unfinished did_post_lasso() unused post_lasso argument two_period_aipw_weights(). Internal helpers longer exported: gt_weights(), mp_weights_obj(), two_period_covs_obj(), mp_covariate_bal_summary_helper(), combine_twfe_weights_gt(), twfe_cov_bal_gt() aipw_cov_bal_gt(). Fewer dependencies: dplyr, tidyr, magrittr, rlang DRDID longer required. caret now required (rather suggested), implicit_twfe_weights() needs BMisc. fix: implicit_twfe_weights() works without covariates (xformula = ~1 NULL). Previously crashed R. Without covariates weights now match twfe_weights(). fix: number post-treatment periods now number observed periods g, max(t) - g + 1. Weights wrong periods skipped. twfe_weights(), attO_weights() att_simple_weights() now return results visibly, print called console. two_period_reg_weights()$est now unnamed number. Clearer error warning messages, name function, requirement alternative one. New vignettes: vignette("twfe-weights") vignette("covariate-balance"). Every exported function now examples, documentation describes function computes returns.
